figure1.prompt:
Create a publication-quality conceptual scientific teaser illustration for an ICML paper about contextual multi-hop reasoning. This is an explanatory conceptual illustration, NOT a numerical data plot or an anatomically precise circuit diagram. Ultra clean white background, very wide horizontal composition approximately 2.8:1, high resolution, crisp flat vector-like drawing, disciplined generous spacing, fine outlines, excellent readable typography at a printed width of 6.75 inches. No textures, photographs, mascots, gradients, shadows, decorative 3D, or fake measured charts. Muted teal #087F8C for successful evidence use, coral #D76B50 for failure, purple #6F5AA8 for the readout, dark charcoal text.

Three horizontally aligned panels separated by subtle light-gray rules; panel headings exactly:
"(a) Correct hops, failed composition"
"(b) Evidence access gates reading"
"(c) Repair using input evidence"

Panel a: top small sentence "Same context, different questions". Show a compact genuine factual chain with three clean boxes: "Walter II of Avesnes" then "James of Avesnes" then "Arsuf". Arrow 1 label "father"; arrow 2 label "died in". Beneath, two short rows with teal check marks: "Hop 1: James of Avesnes" and "Hop 2: Arsuf". Beneath them one coral row with an X: "Composed answer: Avesnes". Avoid extra wording. The chain is factual illustration, not a chart.

Panel b: use an elegant conceptual metaphor of a titled evidence paragraph card labeled "Bridge evidence", with a small purple location pin labeled "Address is recoverable"; below it a narrow faint coral connection labeled "Limited access" feeding an outlined document-reading lens. Alongside, a stronger teal connection labeled "Calibrated access" activates the same document-reading lens, with a bright local phrase highlight labeled "Relation-specific content". This panel illustrates that access and local reading work together; do not draw numbered transformer layers, a literal pipeline of brain stages, or any numerical axes.

Panel c: two original paragraph cards labeled "Root" and "Selected bridge", a small purple selector icon labeled "Input-only selection", then a compact model block labeled "Scoped head adaptation" and a clear teal result pill "Arsuf" with a check mark. Small footer exactly "No support labels at inference". Show selection and adapted answering as conceptual operations, without claiming per-head measured topology.

Overall emphasize one narrative: correct single hops can fail in composition; recoverable evidence location alone is insufficient; selecting original evidence and adapting a small head subset repairs the composed answer. Use only the specified concise labels, accurately spelled. All elements aligned, nothing touching panel boundaries. No caption, no title outside panels, no percentages, no fabricated data.

edits.prompt:
Use case: text-localization.
Asset type: Existing scientific teaser figure for a research paper.
Edit target: the supplied image at paper/figures/figure1_teaser.png.
Primary request: Change ONLY the middle panel's heading. Replace the exact text "(b) Evidence access gates reading" with the exact text "(b) Access and local reading interact".
Preserve every other pixel and visual element as closely as possible: same canvas and aspect ratio, three panel boundaries, all remaining words and their spelling, factual chain, arrows, check marks, icons, colors, typography, font weight, text alignment, backgrounds, spacing, and layout. Do not redraw, embellish, rearrange, add or remove anything else. The new heading must stay entirely within the existing middle-panel header area and match the existing bold black heading style. Keep the white opaque background.

figure2.prompt:
Create an elegant publication-quality conceptual METHOD OVERVIEW illustration for an ICML paper named CoReTrace. Wide horizontal landscape roughly 2.5:1, pure white background, flat vector-like document and attention-head symbols, aligned typography, restrained teal #087F8C, coral #D76B50, purple #6F5AA8, dark charcoal. No measurements, charts, numerical results, neural anatomy, decorative textures, gradients or 3D. This is a conceptual workflow illustration, with exact technical detail provided separately in the manuscript. High readability at 6.75-inch print width.

Use two broad horizontal bands with lots of breathing room:
TOP BAND heading "(a) Offline preparation".
Three equal spacious modules horizontally:
1. "Discover evidence-access heads" with two small document/question icons labeled "Direct hop" and "Composed query", arrows toward a small symbolic head grid with only several teal cells. Subtitle "Paired paragraph-attention gap".
2. "Adapt selected heads" with symbolic Q K V O blocks and a small training page icon. Subtitle "Composed-answer training". Beneath put "Fixed native V/O restoration" with a small shield icon. This denotes fixed prefill restoration, not a learned gate.
3. "Fit the address readout" with a simple purple linear scoring icon above paragraph cards. Subtitle "Training paragraphs only".
A thin divider. Do not show support or answer labels feeding the online band.

BOTTOM BAND heading "(b) Inference from the input".
Left: document stack and question icon labeled "Original context + question".
Arrow to a small root node pointing to two paragraph nodes, labeled "Title-link candidates".
Then a branching concept area with exactly these three clearly separated short rows:
"One candidate: direct choice"
"Several: frozen attention readout"
"No valid root or candidate: keep context"
The first two rows flow to a clean pair of document cards labeled "Root + selected bridge". The third row joins the final model via an unobtrusive gray bypass.
Both routes enter a model block labeled "Scoped head-adapted model", then a small output capsule "Answer".
Small final footer under entire band: "Original paragraph text; no support annotations or answers at inference".
Top readout block has only one subtle purple dashed connector down to "frozen attention readout". Top adaptation block has only one subtle teal dashed connector to the final model. Ensure every arrow is clear and does not cross text.
No more than about 90 words outside these required labels. No title outside band headings, no figure caption. Crisp black sans-serif labels and strong information hierarchy; keep all words and diagrams comfortably inside the canvas.
